{{Short description|Graph showing size of red blood cells}}
{{Orphan|date=October 2025}}

A '''Price-Jones curve''' is a graph showing the [[Histogram|distribution]] of diameters of [[red blood cells]]. Higher diameter may be seen in [[Pernicious anemia|pernicious anaemia]], while lower diameter may be seen after [[haemorrhage]].

== Medical uses ==
A Price-Jones curve can be used in the diagnosis of [[Anemia|anaemia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Sarma |first=P. Ravi |title=Clinical Methods: The History, Physical, and Laboratory Examinations |year=1990 |isbn=978-0-409-90077-4 |edition=3rd |language=en |chapter=152 - Red Cell Indices |pmid=21250103}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=McLaren |first=Christine E |date=June 1996 |title=Mixture models in haematology: a series of case studies |url=https://doi.org/10.1177/096228029600500203 |journal=Statistical Methods in Medical Research |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=129–153 |doi=10.1177/096228029600500203 |pmid=8817795 |s2cid=11124775 |issn=0962-2802|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Price-Jones curves usually vary both by average red blood cell size, and the distribution of sizes.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Evans |first1=Timothy C. |last2=Jehle |first2=Dietrich |date=1991-01-01 |title=The red blood cell distribution width |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0736-4679%2891%2990592-4 |journal=The Journal of Emergency Medicine |language=en |volume=9 |pages=71–74 |doi=10.1016/0736-4679(91)90592-4 |pmid=1955687 |issn=0736-4679|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Interpretation of results ===
Higher red blood cell diameter and wider variation in size are often seen in [[pernicious anaemia]].<ref name=":1" /> Lower diameter with normal variation in size are often seen after [[haemorrhage]].<ref name=":1" /> A higher variation in size is known as [[anisocytosis]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Constantino |first=Benie T. |date=May 2013 |title=Red Cell Distribution Width, Revisited |journal=Laboratory Medicine |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=e2–e9 |doi=10.1309/LMZ1GKY9LQTVFBL7|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Choudhary |first1=Sarita |last2=Bordia |first2=Sandhya |last3=Choudhary |first3=Kavita |date=December 2018 |title=Sensitivity of Red Cell Histogram and CBC parameters against Peripheral Blood Smear in Various Anemias |url=https://www.ijbamr.com/assets/images/issues/pdf/December%202018%20%20135%20-%20141.pdf.pdf |journal=Indian Journal of Basic and Applied Medical Research |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=135–141}}</ref>

== Procedure ==
A [[blood smear]] can be used to view individual [[red blood cell]]s. The diameter of each red blood cell can be measured, which is usually analogous to volume.<ref name=":2" /> This is usually performed automatically by particle counters.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> Data is then converted into a [[histogram]].<ref name=":0" /> This can be used to assess [[red blood cell distribution width]] (RDW).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

== History ==
Cecil Price-Jones first proposed using the Price-Jones curve in a 1922 paper.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Price-Jones |first=Cecil |date=1922 |title=The diameters of red cells in pernicious anaemia and in anaemia following haemorrhage |url=https://ia800708.us.archive.org/view_archive.php?archive=/28/items/crossref-pre-1923-scholarly-works/10.1002%252Fpath.1700190105.zip&file=10.1002%252Fpath.1700250410.pdf |journal=The Journal of Pathology and Bacteriology |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=487–504|doi=10.1002/path.1700250410 }}</ref> It has been used for assessing [[red blood cell]]s since then.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Halie |first=M. R. |date=1985 |title=Aspects of quantitative cytometry: an overview |journal=[[Pure and Applied Chemistry]] |language=de |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=587–592 |doi=10.1351/pac198557040587 |s2cid=54866239 |issn=1365-3075|doi-access=free }}</ref>
